research.area: Gemma 4 model family and runtimes (as of 2026-10-18)

findings.claim: The Gemma 4 lineup today is E2B (2.3B effective / 5.1B with PLE), E4B (4.5B / 8B), 12B Unified (11.95B, encoder-free), 26B-A4B MoE (25.2B total / 3.8B active) and 31B dense, released 2026-03-31 (E2B/E4B/26B/31B), 2026-04-16 (MTP drafters), 2026-06-03 (12B Unified), plus DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B (2026-06-10) and EmbeddingGemma 2 740M (2026-10-06); there is no 270M-class Gemma 4.
findings.evidence: Google's release log lists exactly those four entries (Mar 31, Apr 16, Jun 3, Oct 6); the model card table gives per-model layers/params/context; the HF launch blog lists the repos including diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it.

findings.claim: Audio input exists only on E2B, E4B and 12B Unified; 26B-A4B and 31B are text+image; every Gemma 4 model outputs text only (no model generates speech), video is handled as frames (model card: max 60 s at 1 fps; 12B guide: 70 visual tokens/frame), and context is 128K for E2B/E4B and 256K for the others.
findings.evidence: Model card: 'Audio supports a maximum length of 30 seconds', input modalities per row, output 'text'; 12B developer guide shows 313 frames at 1 FPS with a 70-token budget. A separate TTS (e.g. Kokoro or Kyutai Pocket TTS, both used in Jetson demos) is therefore mandatory for a talking robot.

findings.claim: E2B/E4B audio goes through a 305M-parameter USM-style Conformer (12 layers, 40 ms frames, 128 mel bins, 16 kHz, continuous embeddings, ~25 tokens per second of audio, hard 30 s cap = 750 audio tokens), and the supported tasks are ASR and speech-to-translated-text (transcribe-then-translate), not open-ended audio dialogue.
findings.evidence: Technical report section on audio (305M conformer, 40 ms chunks, 87 MB quantized); Transformers Gemma4Processor defaults audio_seq_length=750, audio_ms_per_token=40, feature extractor sampling_rate=16000, max_length=480000 samples with truncation.

findings.claim: Multilingual speech is decent but not Whisper-large class: FLEURS WER avg 0.090 (E2B) / 0.075 (E4B) / ~0.069 (12B, ex-zh) with per-language E2B/E4B WER en 0.080/0.065, es 0.042/0.035, it 0.041/0.032, de 0.076/0.061, fr 0.101/0.080, hi 0.101/0.086, ru 0.084/0.068, ar 0.143/0.162, and CER ko 0.066/0.053, ja 0.107/0.078, zh 0.187/0.136; CoVoST X→en BLEU avg 35.4 (E2B) / 38.2 (E4B); Google claims 35+ languages out of the box, 140+ pretrained.
findings.evidence: Tables in the Gemma 4 technical report (v2, July 2026) and the model card. Community English check via llama-server on LibriSpeech test-other: E2B-BF16 13.15% WER vs Whisper large-v3-turbo 11.48%, RTF 0.038 on a desktop CUDA GPU (DEV post, May 2026, community).

findings.claim: Gemma 4 is released under Apache 2.0 (not the Gemma Terms of Use), so hackathon, demo and commercial use are unrestricted beyond Apache's notice requirements; EmbeddingGemma 2 and DiffusionGemma are also Apache 2.0.
findings.evidence: HF model cards list 'License: apache-2.0'; Google's blog calls it 'a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license'; ai.google.dev's Gemma Terms page says 'For Gemma 4 terms, see the Gemma 4 license' and its appendix of covered models excludes Gemma 4; the linked Gemma 4 license page is the Apache 2.0 text. Google still links a Prohibited Use Policy from the docs, so keep the demo within it.

findings.claim: Thinking is toggled by placing the <|think|> token in the system turn; output is <|channel>thought ... <channel|> then the answer, E2B/E4B emit no thought block when thinking is off (larger models emit an empty one), and runtimes expose it as enable_thinking (Transformers/llama.cpp chat_template_kwargs), --reasoning-parser gemma4 (vLLM), ThinkingConfig(enable_thinking, thinking_token_budget) (LiteRT-LM Python).
findings.evidence: Official prompt-formatting page and model card describe the token and channel format; vLLM recipe and LiteRT-LM Python docs name the flags; a Jetson project notes llama-server needs --reasoning off or Gemma 4 spends its budget thinking and returns empty content.

findings.claim: Native tool use is a trained format with six control tokens (<|tool>…<tool|> declarations, <|tool_call>…<tool_call|>, <|tool_response>…<tool_response|>) plus a <|"|> string delimiter; the model emits e.g. <|tool_call>call:get_weather{city:<|"|>Bangkok<|"|>}<tool_call|>, tools are passed as OpenAI-style JSON schemas through the chat template, and llama.cpp (--jinja), vLLM (--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4) and LiteRT-LM (Python functions with docstrings/type hints as tools=[...]) parse it natively.
findings.evidence: Official prompt-formatting page lists the tokens and call/response syntax; HF blog shows the raw E4B output; LiteRT-LM API overview documents automatic tool execution in Python/Kotlin/Swift/JS. The harness CLAUDE.md already notes the template sorts arguments alphabetically and enums/ranges are not grammar-enforced.

findings.claim: llama.cpp supports Gemma 4 E2B/E4B audio since PR #21421 (merged 2026-04-12; follow-up #21625 for clips over ~17 s; a load regression #24084 was fixed 2026-06-04 by #24091), the ggml-org E2B/E4B GGUFs are listed as 'mixed (audio + vision)' mmproj, and llama-server takes audio through the OpenAI-compatible input_audio content part (data or url; wav/mp3/flac auto-detected; the format field is ignored).
findings.evidence: PR #21421 adds the USM conformer with 30-s chunking, tested on CPU/Vulkan/CUDA, and recommends a BF16 mmproj because F16/Q8_0 projectors caused repetition; docs/multimodal.md and tools/server/README.md document the model list and the input_audio part. Local verification on this Mac: the cached unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-GGUF mmproj-BF16.gguf (986.8 MB, the exact file run_llama.sh loads) and google/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf/gemma-4-E4B-it-mmproj.gguf (991.6 MB) both have clip.has_audio_encoder=true, clip.audio.projector_type=gemma4a, 12 blocks, 128 mel bins, 751 'a.*' tensors, so the existing harness server can accept speech with no new downloads.

findings.claim: Audio into Gemma 4 E2B via llama.cpp on a Jetson Orin is demonstrated by community code but flagged by NVIDIA: the Jetson AI Lab tutorial says llama.cpp has 'a known audio issue with E2B on Orin' and recommends vLLM for audio, while dwain-barnes/jetson-voice-assistant runs native audio into E2B on an Orin Nano Super (llama.cpp commit 9f0d017, CUDA arch 87, unsloth mmproj-F16, -ngl 99, --reasoning off, ctx 2048) with 0.37–0.56 s time-to-first-token and a 5.65 GiB GPU budget (Q4 2.97 GiB + projector 0.92 GiB + KV 0.25 GiB).
findings.evidence: Jetson AI Lab 'Gemma 4 on Jetson' page (JetPack 6 / L4T r36 for Orin; recommends E2B/E4B on Orin NX); the community repo README lists build flags, latencies and NvMap/page-cache pitfalls. Neither source names the specific llama.cpp issue, so it must be tested on PC2.

findings.claim: LiteRT-LM is at v0.18.0 (2026-10-06) and on Linux/macOS/Windows/Android/Raspberry Pi provides: Python 'litert-lm-api' (Engine(path, backend=Backend.CPU|GPU|NPU, audio_backend=..., vision_backend=..., enable_speculative_decoding=True), Contents.of(text, Content.AudioFile(...)/ImageFile(...)), tools=[python functions], ThinkingConfig), a CLI ('litert-lm run --backend=gpu --attachment=audio.wav --audio-backend=gpu --preset=preset.py' for an automatic tool loop; 'litert-lm import'; 'litert-lm describe'), and 'litert-lm serve' (OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/models on port 9379).
findings.evidence: GitHub README 'What's New' and releases page (v0.14.0 added GPU/NPU audio acceleration and reasoning channels; v0.15 AutoToolChat; v0.17.0 Gemma 4 12B multimodal + MTP; v0.18.0 EmbeddingGemma 2, import, serve /v1/embeddings); developers.google.com Python, CLI usage and OpenAI-server pages give the exact APIs/flags. Linux GPU uses Vulkan drivers per the CLI usage page; issue #1848 shows Linux CPU audio works once audio_backend is set (3-s WAV in 5.4 s on a 4 GB x86 box).

findings.claim: Official .litertlm bundles exist for Gemma 4 E2B (gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm 2588 MB with vision+audio loaded on demand; -gpu/-web 2008 MB text-only; NPU builds for Qualcomm QCS8275/SM8750, Google Tensor G5/G6, Intel LNL/PTL), E4B (3660 MB full; 2969 MB gpu/web), 12B (6883 MB, needs LiteRT-LM ≥0.17) and EmbeddingGemma 2 (485 MB generic plus Qualcomm/MediaTek/Tensor/Intel NPU builds); there is no NVIDIA-specific build, and the GPU path on linux_arm64 is a WebGPU accelerator only (no CUDA/Vulkan/OpenCL libs).
findings.evidence: File trees from the litert-community repos (listed via the HF API on 2026-10-18); the E2B card says 'the Vision and Audio models are loaded on demand' and the web build 'is text-only'; issue #2570 states linux_arm64 ships only libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so.

findings.claim: LiteRT-LM on Jetson Orin is officially benchmarked but unreliable: Google's E2B card lists Jetson Orin Nano GPU at 1,142 prefill / 24.2 decode tok/s with 0.9 s TTFT (CPU 109 / 12.2), yet issue #2570 (opened 2026-06-15, closed 2026-07-01 without a verified fix, still reproduced 2026-08-16) shows the WebGPU backend crashing during delegate compilation on Orin (L4T R36) and Thor with v0.13.1–0.14, and a 2026-09-14 comment reports it working on an Orin NX 16 GB only after downloading prebuilt/linux_arm64 and running LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./linux_arm64 litert-lm run --backend=gpu; issue #2001 confirmed the pip wheel's Backend.GPU worked on Orin NX in April (≈1.9 s per short prompt, +1.2 GB RAM).
findings.evidence: Benchmark table on the litert-community E2B card; both GitHub issues with dates, versions and the workaround. Net: a LiteRT-LM-on-Orin demo is feasible but must be proven on PC2 on day one, with the CPU backend (E2B ~12 tok/s class) as the fallback.

findings.claim: NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM lists Gemma 4 E2B/E4B/12B as text+image+audio and 26B-A4B/31B as text+image with paired MTP 'assistant' checkpoints (page updated 2026-09-29), Orin supports only FP16/INT8/INT4 engines, and community measurements on an Orin NX 16 GB give ~31.7 tok/s decode for E2B and ~24.3 tok/s for W4A16 E4B, but the FP16 token+PLE embedding tables (5.13 GiB E2B, 6.50 GiB E4B) leave only ~3.1 GB MemAvailable with E4B until the open INT8-sidecar issue #188 lands.
findings.evidence: Edge-LLM supported-models page and support matrix; issue #188 (opened 2026-08-22; maintainer on 2026-10-09: 'We will work on consolidating this feature in our future release'), which also reports E2B TTFT 485 ms on an 8 GB Orin Nano.

findings.claim: vLLM supports Gemma 4 audio only for E2B/E4B (Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration) and all modalities for 12B (Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration), served with 'vllm serve google/gemma-4-E4B-it --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 --limit-mm-per-prompt image=N,audio=M' (install vllm[audio]; audio as an audio_url part), and NVIDIA ships Jetson containers ghcr.io/nvidia-ai-iot/vllm:gemma4-jetson-orin (JetPack 6) that Jetson AI Lab recommends for audio on Orin; the recipe's 24 GB+ GPU-memory guidance for BF16 E2B/E4B makes this a tight fit on a 16 GB NX.
findings.evidence: vLLM Gemma 4 recipe and supported-models page; Jetson AI Lab tutorial commands and model table (unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF:Q4_K_S for llama.cpp, google/gemma-4-E2B-it for vLLM on Orin).

findings.claim: Ollama's gemma4 library exposes text+image input for every tag and its Gemma 4 audio path is still broken (issue #15333, GGML assert during audio inference, open since 2026-04-05 with no linked fix), and Jetson AI Lab says Gemma 4 'does not currently work on Orin Nano with Ollama', so Ollama is not a viable audio runtime for the robot.
findings.evidence: ollama.com/library/gemma4 lists 'Text, Image' per tag (audio only as a tag word); the Ollama issue page shows no assignee, PR or milestone; the June note.com write-up still lists #15333 as open.

findings.claim: On the Mac, mlx-vlm runs Gemma 4 E2B/E4B audio ('mlx_vlm.generate --model google/gemma-4-e2b-it --audio file.wav --prompt "Transcribe this audio"'), and mlx-swift-lm ported the gemma4_audio USM-Conformer (PR #392), but the 26B/31B MLX variants have no audio tower; early MLX audio bugs (silently ignored audio) were reported around launch.
findings.evidence: Simon Willison's 2026-04-12 post shows a 14-s voice memo transcribed with minor word errors; the mlx-swift-lm PR and community Swift port confirm E2B/E4B only.

findings.claim: Hugging Face Transformers (docs current at v5.20.1) loads Gemma 4 with AutoModelForMultimodalLM / Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration and Gemma4Processor (image_seq_length default 280 with options 70/140/280/560/1120, images sized to multiples of 48, audio_seq_length 750 at 40 ms/token), passes audio as {"type":"audio","url":...}, tools via apply_chat_template(tools=[...]), thinking via enable_thinking=True, and parses output with processor.parse_response; Google's ordering guidance is images before the text and audio after the text.
findings.evidence: Transformers model_doc page (classes, processor defaults, feature-extractor settings) and the HF launch blog (tool example, ordering note, load_audio_from_video=True for E2B/E4B video-with-audio).

findings.claim: There are no open-weight Gemma robotics models: Gemini Robotics 2, Gemini Robotics-ER 2 and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 (announced 2026-07-30; On-Device 2 is 'based on Gemini Robotics 1.5 technology and our on-device Gemma models', bi-arm, evaluated on SO101/Dexmate) are trusted-tester/early-access only, Google's 2026-09-22 'Android of robotics' open-sourcing is Intrinsic Core (industrial arms, ROS, Apache 2.0), and the open path for the G1 is LeRobot's official Unitree G1 support (29/23-DoF, Homunculus exoskeleton teleop, lerobot-record, pi0.5 fine-tuning, lerobot-rollout with RTC, GR00T/Holosoma locomotion controllers; docs dated March 2026).
findings.evidence: DeepMind On-Device 2 model card ('currently available to a select group of trusted testers'), Gemini Robotics 2 blog (no Gemma, SDK, LeRobot or open weights mentioned), Forbes/Yahoo coverage of Intrinsic Core, LeRobot unitree_g1 docs.

findings.claim: What Google/NVIDIA are showcasing for Gemma 4 on robots right now is exactly an edge voice+vision agent: @googlegemma (post ~late Aug 2026) touts 'Gemma 4 E2B running fully locally on an 8GB NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano… native image/audio input and function calling… vision, voice interaction, and camera control', and NVIDIA's HF blog (2026-04-22, Asier Arranz) publishes the reference stack Parakeet STT → Gemma 4 E2B Q4_K_M on llama-server (--jinja, -c 2048, --image-min-tokens 70 --image-max-tokens 70, -ngl 99, --flash-attn on, --no-mmproj-offload, -np 1) → a single look_and_answer webcam tool the model invokes on its own → Kokoro TTS; adjacent Gemma-team pushes are AI Edge Gallery 'Agent Skills' (SKILL.md + run_js/run_intent tools), Gemma 4 inside Android AICore as Gemini Nano, and EmbeddingGemma 2 (191 MB text-only / 567 MB all-modality RAM on Pixel 11 Pro, 37 ms per image on an M5 Pro GPU, served via litert-lm serve /v1/embeddings).
findings.evidence: Search snippet of the X post (full post not fetchable), NVIDIA HF blog and asierarranz/Google_Gemma repo, developers.googleblog agentic-skills post and gallery/skills README, EmbeddingGemma 2 edge blog, litert-community E2B card ('available through Android AI Core as Gemini Nano').

findings.claim: Multi-token-prediction drafters ship for every Gemma 4 size (GGUF mtp-*.gguf of 59 MB Q4_0 auto-picked by recent llama.cpp with --spec-type draft-mtp; LiteRT-LM --enable-speculative-decoding, which Google calls 'universally recommended' on GPU with >2x mobile-GPU decode; Edge-LLM 'assistant' checkpoints), but the harness measured MTP as a net loss on the M4 Pro and Orin gains are unmeasured.
findings.evidence: Release log 2026-04-16; unsloth QAT README MTP section (Jun 9 update); LiteRT-LM Python docs; LATENCY_RESULTS.md (95 vs 113 tok/s).

research.digest:
What exists. Gemma 4 (Apache 2.0, so no license worries for a hackathon demo or a product) is five models: E2B, E4B, 12B Unified, 26B-A4B MoE, 31B, released March 31 2026 with the 12B added June 3 and EmbeddingGemma 2 (740M, text+image+video+audio embeddings) on October 6. Only E2B, E4B and 12B hear audio; nothing in the family speaks, so a TTS (Kokoro or Kyutai Pocket TTS are the proven Jetson choices) is a separate component. Audio is clip-based, not streaming: 16 kHz, 40 ms per token, hard 30 s cap, trained for transcription and transcribe-then-translate. Quality is "good small ASR" rather than Whisper-large: FLEURS WER 0.090 (E2B) / 0.075 (E4B), best in Spanish/Italian/Portuguese (0.03-0.06), weakest in Arabic and Chinese (CER 0.19 for E2B), X-to-English CoVoST BLEU 35/38. E4B is roughly 15-25% better at speech than E2B across the board, which matters for a multilingual concierge. Thinking is a <|think|> system token; tool calls are a trained six-token format that llama.cpp (--jinja), vLLM (--tool-call-parser gemma4) and LiteRT-LM all parse natively. Video is frames at 1 fps (70 tokens/frame budget).

What runs where. The best news for us is verified locally: the exact mmproj-BF16.gguf the harness already loads (unsloth E2B QAT) and Google's official E4B QAT mmproj both carry the gemma4a audio encoder (751 audio tensors, 12 conformer blocks), and llama.cpp has supported Gemma 4 audio since April 12 (PR #21421, regression fixed June 4). So run_llama.sh as it stands can accept a WAV through the OpenAI-compatible input_audio part today; the PR recommends keeping the projector at BF16 and the harness should disable thinking (E2B otherwise burns its budget and returns empty content). On the Orin the picture is mixed: NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab says llama.cpp has "a known audio issue with E2B on Orin" and points to its vLLM container, while a community Orin Nano Super project runs native speech into E2B on llama.cpp CUDA (arch 87) with 0.4-0.6 s time-to-first-token in a 5.7 GiB GPU budget. Treat that as the first thing to test on PC2. TensorRT Edge-LLM lists E2B/E4B/12B with audio and measures ~32 tok/s (E2B) and ~24 tok/s (E4B W4A16) decode on an Orin NX 16 GB, but E4B's FP16 embedding tables leave only ~3 GB free, so on the NX prefer E2B, or E4B only if nothing else needs memory. Ollama's audio path is still crashing (issue open since April) and it does not run Gemma 4 on Orin Nano at all; skip it. MLX and Transformers both do audio and are fine for Mac-side development.

LiteRT-LM (v0.18.0, Oct 6) is production-quality on phones, laptops and Raspberry Pi, has a clean Python API (Engine with backend/audio_backend/vision_backend, Content.AudioFile, Python functions as tools, ThinkingConfig), a CLI with --attachment=audio.wav and an automatic tool loop, and an OpenAI-compatible serve mode. Official E2B/E4B/12B bundles exist with on-demand vision+audio, plus NPU builds for Qualcomm, Tensor G5/G6 and Intel; there is no NVIDIA build. On Jetson it is officially benchmarked (Orin Nano GPU: 24 tok/s decode, 0.9 s TTFT) but the linux_arm64 GPU path is a WebGPU accelerator that users reported crashing on Orin from June through August; a September report says it works on an Orin NX 16 GB after manually fetching the prebuilt/linux_arm64 libraries. CPU fallback works but is ~12 tok/s class.

Robotics. There is no open Gemma robotics model: Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 (July 30) is Gemma-based but trusted-tester only, bi-arm, and explicitly weak on high-DoF bodies. The open route for a G1 is LeRobot's official Unitree G1 support (teleop with an exoskeleton, record, pi0.5 fine-tune, RTC rollout), which is a multi-day data effort, not a six-day one.

Recommendation. Make Gemma 4 the whole cognitive loop, which is exactly what the Gemma team is showcasing right now (their late-August post: E2B on an 8 GB Orin Nano with native image/audio input, function calling, voice interaction and camera control; NVIDIA's reference stack is Parakeet STT -> E2B -> look_and_answer tool -> Kokoro). We can beat that reference by removing the STT: feed the microphone clip straight into Gemma (VAD-chunked under 30 s, audio placed after the text, image before it), let one model transcribe, understand, pick a language, and emit the robot tool call, and keep the measured sub-second perception path for navigation. Use E2B on PC2 for latency and memory headroom, E4B only if speech accuracy in non-English demos needs it. For the LiteRT prize, do not bet the robot on LiteRT-LM-on-Orin; instead put LiteRT-LM where it is solid and judge-visible: EmbeddingGemma 2 via litert-lm serve as the robot's multimodal memory ("where did you see my keys?", search over what the camera and microphone captured), and/or Gemma 4 E2B on a Pixel/Raspberry Pi as the concierge front-end that talks to the robot over the LAN. Test LiteRT-LM GPU on PC2 on day one anyway; if it runs, that becomes the headline. Judges from the Gemma team will respond to: native audio in, native tool calling, EmbeddingGemma 2 (two weeks old), everything offline, and measured latencies on the slide.
open_questions: Does audio input actually work on llama.cpp CUDA on the Orin NX (Jetson AI Lab claims a 'known audio issue with E2B on Orin' without citing it)? Test in <1 h on PC2: build llama.cpp master with -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=87, copy the cached unsloth E2B QAT GGUF + mmproj-BF16.gguf from the Mac (~3.6 GB, no new download), start llama-server with --jinja -np 1 -c 4096 and send a 3-s 16 kHz WAV as an input_audio part; if it aborts, retry with --no-mmproj-offload and with the ggml-org mmproj-gemma-4-E2B-it-BF16.gguf.

Audio latency on the Orin is unmeasured: a desktop CUDA GPU showed real-time factor 0.038 and Linux x86 CPU LiteRT-LM took 5.4 s for a 3-s clip. Measure wall time for 2 s / 5 s / 15 s clips through llama-server on PC2 and decide whether a VAD-chunked 'listen while the robot walks' design is viable.

Does LiteRT-LM v0.18 GPU (WebGPU) run on PC2 (JetPack 6.2 / L4T 36.4.3)? Test: uv tool install litert-lm; fetch the prebuilt/linux_arm64 directory from the LiteRT-LM GitHub release; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./linux_arm64 litert-lm run --backend=gpu --from-huggingface-repo=litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm --attachment=test.wav --audio-backend=cpu --prompt='Transcribe'. Fall back to --backend=cpu and record tok/s for both.

Does 'litert-lm serve' accept image_url / input_audio parts in /v1/chat/completions? The docs only show text; verify with one curl against the local server, otherwise use the Python API for multimodal and serve only embeddings.

Audio + image in the same Gemma 4 turn on llama.cpp (mixed mmproj) is documented but untested here; verify one request with both parts and check for the known repetition/looping failure mode and the 30-s truncation.

Multilingual accuracy in a noisy demo room with accented speakers is unmeasured (one secondhand report cites ~41% WER for Gemma 4 on AMI meeting audio vs ~16% for Whisper large-v3). Record 10 utterances per demo language (e.g. English, Spanish, Mandarin, Japanese) with the intended microphone and score E2B vs E4B before choosing the model size.
Which Transformers release first added Gemma 4 could not be pinned (docs are at v5.20.1; cards say 'latest'); irrelevant unless we fine-tune.

The runtime behind Google's late-August Jetson Orin Nano tweet (native audio + function calling + camera control) is unknown; the only public reference stack (NVIDIA HF blog) uses llama.cpp with a separate Parakeet STT. If the Gemma team's own demo code surfaces, mirror its prompt/tool structure.

TensorRT Edge-LLM on a 16 GB NX: E4B leaves ~3.1 GB headroom and E2B ~5.9 GB with FP16 embedding sidecars (issue #188 still open); only worth pursuing if llama.cpp decode on PC2 is too slow for the tool-call budget.
Web-search budget ran out before verifying a NVIDIA-forum LiteRT-LM vs llama.cpp Jetson Thor benchmark (forum returned 403); it is Thor-only and not needed for Orin decisions.

checks.claim: Audio input exists only on E2B, E4B and 12B Unified; 26B-A4B and 31B are text+image; all Gemma 4 models output text only; video = frames (max 60 s at 1 fps; 12B guide 70 visual tokens/frame); context 128K (E2B/E4B) and 256K (others).
checks.note: Model card table (ai.google.dev copy last updated 2026-07-30, and the identical gemma.ai copy): E2B/E4B/12B Unified = text, image, audio; 26B A4B and 31B = text, image; 128K/128K/256K/256K/256K; models are 'generating text output'; 'Audio supports a maximum length of 30 seconds'; 'Video supports a maximum of 60 seconds assuming the images are processed at one frame per second'. 12B developer guide: frames extracted at 1 FPS, 313 frames for a 5-minute segment, 'visual token budget of 70 tokens per frame'; 12B is 'our first medium-sized model with audio input'. Extra facts: 12B 'Unified' means encoder-free (raw audio waveform projected into the LLM embedding space; 31B has no audio); the ai.google.dev docs now carry a banner 'This documentation is deprecated. Please visit the new documentation at gemma.ai'; HF transformers' Gemma4VideoProcessor defaults num_frames=32 and max_soft_tokens per frame in {70,140,280,560,1120}. The technical report itself states no context window (only 128k/256k eval settings); the 128K/256K figures come from the model card and launch blog.

checks.claim: E2B/E4B audio encoder: 305M USM-style Conformer, 12 layers, 40 ms frames, 128 mel bins, 16 kHz, ~25 tokens per second, hard 30 s cap = 750 audio tokens.
checks.note: Gemma 4 Technical Report arXiv:2607.02770v2 (24 Jul 2026), Sec. 2.2: 'E2B and E4B Gemma models use a 305M audio encoder that processes audio in 40ms chunks with Mel filterbank inputs', 'two downsampling convolution layers followed by twelve Conformer layers', parameter count cut 'from 680M to 305M', quantized size 'from 390 MB in Gemma 3n to 87 MB'. The report does not state mel bins, tokens/s or a 30 s limit; those come from elsewhere: transformers Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor feature_size=128, sampling_rate=16000, frame 20 ms / hop 10 ms, max_length=480000 samples (=30 s) with truncation=True; Gemma4Processor audio_seq_length=750, audio_ms_per_token=40 ('SSCP convolution's 4x time reduction on 10ms frames'); gemma.ai audio guide: 'Each second of audio is 25 tokens for Gemma 4' and audio must be mono, 16 kHz. Local GGUF header parse of both cached projectors: clip.audio.block_count=12, clip.audio.num_mel_bins=128, embedding 1024, 8 heads. Live llama-server test on this Mac matched 25 tok/s (1.58 s clip -> 51 prompt tokens incl. ~11 template tokens; 2.91 s -> 90 incl. text prompt; 4.27 s -> 124). Note the 12B Unified path differs: raw 40 ms chunks at 16 kHz -> 640-dim vectors projected directly into the LLM. Note also llama.cpp PR #21421 splits audio >30 s into 30 s segments, whereas HF truncates at 30 s.

checks.claim: The supported audio tasks are ASR and speech-to-translated-text (transcribe-then-translate), not open-ended audio dialogue.
checks.note: The ASR/AST wording is what the official docs list as the trained and benchmarked tasks (model card: 'Automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech-to-translated-text translation across multiple languages'; tech report evaluates only FLEURS ASR and CoVoST S2TT). But the model is not limited to those tasks in practice: the model card also says E2B/E4B/12B 'can analyze and interpret audio inputs, enabling voice-driven interactions and transcriptions'; the launch blog says 'native audio input for speech recognition and understanding'; the gemma.ai audio guide demonstrates a five-clip prompt 'Give me a concise overview of these audio files'; the dwain-barnes Jetson assistant feeds microphone audio straight into E2B and gets answers. Live test here (E2B UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj-BF16, thinking off, greedy): spoken 'What is the capital of France?' + 'Answer the question asked in the audio in one short sentence.' -> 'The capital of France is Paris.' (232 ms wall); same clip with NO text prompt -> 'Paris'; spoken 'Please bring me a cold can of soda from the fridge in the kitchen.' with a JSON instruction -> {"object": "cold can of soda", "location": "fridge"} (401 ms). Caveat from the same session (n=1, synthetic macOS TTS voice): Spanish transcription was slightly wrong ('...refresco de lon.' for '...de la nevera') and the English translation was garbage ('Oh robot, pour the water, la de refresco de lon ever.'), so spoken-command understanding works in English but multilingual S2TT on E2B needs per-language evaluation, not assumption.

checks.claim: FLEURS WER avg 0.090 (E2B) / 0.075 (E4B) / ~0.069 (12B ex-zh) with the listed per-language WER/CER, CoVoST X->en BLEU 35.4 / 38.2, 35+ languages out of the box and 140+ pretrained; community LibriSpeech check E2B-BF16 13.15% vs Whisper large-v3-turbo 11.48%, RTF 0.038.
checks.note: Every per-language figure matches tech report Table 7 verbatim (en 0.080/0.065, ko* 0.066/0.053, ja* 0.107/0.078, de 0.076/0.061, fr 0.101/0.080, hi 0.101/0.086, es 0.042/0.035, it 0.041/0.032, pt-br 0.056/0.046, ru 0.084/0.068, ar 0.143/0.162, zh* 0.187/0.136, AVG 0.090/0.075; * = CER). The 12B 0.069 (excluding Chinese) is from the model card. CoVoST X->en averages 35.4/38.2 are the tech report's Table 7 numbers, BUT the official model card lists different CoVoST values: 33.47 (E2B), 35.54 (E4B), 38.5* (12B); both are Google sources and the discrepancy is unexplained (likely different subsets), so cite one consistently. '35+ languages out of the box, pre-trained on 140+ languages' is on the model card. Community check (DEV post dated May 27, internal dates 2026): llama-server build b9297 (win-cuda-13.1), LibriSpeech test-other, only 50 samples: Gemma 4 E2B-it-BF16 WER 13.15% / CER 4.95%, RTF 0.038; Whisper LargeV3Turbo WER 11.48% on CUDA (10.15% on Vulkan), RTF 0.055; GPU model not named; E2B-Q8_0 was unstable (stray <|channel> tokens, 19.22% WER); 'Gemma 4 audio is bounded at 30 seconds per request'. Small n, so treat 'not Whisper-large class' as indicative, not established.

checks.claim: Gemma 4 is released under Apache 2.0 (not the Gemma Terms of Use); EmbeddingGemma 2 and DiffusionGemma are also Apache 2.0.
checks.note: Model card: license 'Apache 2.0'; HF google/gemma-4-E4B-it 'License: apache-2.0'; Google launch blog (Apr 02, 2026): 'released under a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license'; ai.google.dev/gemma/terms (last modified April 1, 2026): 'For Gemma 4 terms, see the Gemma 4 license' linking /gemma/apache_2, which is the plain Apache License 2.0 text with no Gemma-specific additions, and the Terms' appendix of covered models lists neither Gemma 4, EmbeddingGemma 2 nor DiffusionGemma. The cached GGUF projectors carry general.license=apache-2.0 and general.license.link=https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license (also the Apache text). HF API: google/embeddinggemma-2 and google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it are tagged license:apache-2.0. The model-card sidebar still links 'Prohibited use'; that policy is incorporated by reference into the Gemma Terms (which exclude Gemma 4), so for Gemma 4 it is guidance rather than a contractual restriction (not legal advice). New canonical license page: gemma.ai/resources/apache-2/.

checks.claim: llama.cpp supports Gemma 4 E2B/E4B audio since PR #21421 (merged 2026-04-12; follow-up #21625 for clips over ~17 s; load regression #24084 fixed 2026-06-04 by #24091); ggml-org E2B/E4B listed as mixed audio+vision; llama-server takes input_audio (data or url; wav/mp3/flac auto-detected; format ignored); the cached unsloth E2B mmproj-BF16 and google E4B mmproj both contain the audio encoder so the harness server can accept speech with no new downloads.
checks.note: PR #21421 'mtmd: add Gemma 4 audio conformer encoder support' (author stephencox-ict) merged by ngxson Apr 12, 2026; closes issue #21325; USM-style Conformer, 30-second chunking, tested CPU/Vulkan/CUDA; other sample rates are 'downsampled using miniaudio's linear resampler' (feed 16 kHz). Corrections: #21625 ('model: fix multimodal padding token for gemma3n/gemma4') merged Apr 9, 2026, i.e. a prerequisite extracted from #21421, not a follow-up; #21421 says it improves reliability for audio around 17 s and longer. The 'use BF16 mmproj, F16/Q8_0 cause repetition' advice is outdated: ngxson traced the repetition to causal attention set incorrectly and fixed it in #21824 (merged Apr 13, 2026), after which Q8_0 works; ggml-org ships mmproj BF16 (987 MB) and Q8_0 (557 MB), unsloth ships BF16/F16/F32; #23815 (rms norm eps) merged May 28; #24084 'llama-server SIGABRT when loading Gemma 4 mmproj with audio encoder' (regression from #24077, opened Jun 3) fixed by #24091 merged Jun 4, 2026. Metal: the PR's test list omitted Metal and ggml_roll fell back to CPU then (#21782, closed unmerged), but current master's ggml-metal-device.cpp supports GGML_OP_ROLL (contiguous) with a kernel_roll pipeline. docs/multimodal.md lists E2B/E4B under 'Mixed modalities' with 'Capabilities: audio input, vision input' (not the literal phrase 'mixed (audio + vision)'); tools/server/README.md: 'Either input_audio.data or input_audio.url can be specified', 'Accepts formats supported by miniaudio (mp3, wav, flac)', 'input_audio.format will be ignored, the file format will be determined automatically', local files need --media-path and a file:// prefix; multimodal is marked experimental. Local checks: GGUF header parse of mmproj-BF16.gguf (986,833,728 bytes) and gemma-4-E4B-it-mmproj.gguf (991,552,256 bytes): clip.has_audio_encoder=true, clip.audio.projector_type=gemma4a, 12 blocks, 128 mel bins, 751 'a.*' tensors (plus 658 'v.*'); the HF manifest for unsloth/...:UD-Q4_K_XL has a projector layer of exactly 986,833,728 bytes, so run_llama.sh's -hf line auto-loads that BF16 projector. Live test via bench/serve.sh (local llama 0.4.0-dev build 10909, commit a2878d30d of 2026-09-11, -np 1 --cache-ram 0 -c 4096 --swa-full): a 2.9 s English clip was transcribed verbatim, prompt 90 tokens in 351 ms, 16 output tokens, 511 ms wall; server log warns 'audio input is in experimental stage and may have reduced quality'. Re-sending identical audio hit the KV cache (cached_tokens=113), so the CLAUDE.md rule against timing repeated identical images applies equally to audio clips.

checks.claim: Audio into Gemma 4 E2B via llama.cpp on Jetson Orin: NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab tutorial says llama.cpp has 'a known audio issue with E2B on Orin' and recommends vLLM; dwain-barnes/jetson-voice-assistant runs native audio into E2B on an Orin Nano Super (llama.cpp 9f0d017, CUDA arch 87, unsloth mmproj-F16, -ngl 99, --reasoning off, ctx 2048) with 0.37-0.56 s TTFT and a 5.65 GiB budget (Q4 2.97 + projector 0.92 + KV 0.25 GiB); neither names the specific issue.
checks.note: Jetson AI Lab 'Gemma 4 on Jetson': exact wording is 'There is currently an audio issue with E2B under llama.cpp.' and 'If audio is important for your setup, use the small Gemma 4 models through vLLM.' (no 'known', no date, no link, E2B named only; E4B under llama.cpp not addressed). Same page: JP6/L4T r36.x for Orin, JP7/r38.x for Thor; E2B/E4B are 'the natural choices' for Orin NX; containers ghcr.io/nvidia-ai-iot/vllm:gemma4-jetson-orin and ghcr.io/nvidia-ai-iot/llama_cpp:latest-jetson-orin; vLLM needs --reasoning-parser gemma4 --tool-call-parser gemma4; Ollama does not currently work with Gemma 4 on Orin Nano. vLLM's supported-models page lists Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration with inputs T + I+ + V + A* (audio only E2B/E4B) and Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration T + I+ + V + A. dwain-barnes repo (14 commits, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-01): Orin Nano Super 8 GB, JetPack 6 L4T R36.4.7, llama.cpp pinned at 9f0d017 ('mtmd: harden preprocessor_granite', 2026-08-17, i.e. after every audio fix above), CUDA arch 87, unsloth mmproj-F16 (~0.92 GiB), -ngl 99, contextSize 2048, --reasoning off described as mandatory (empty content otherwise); TTFT 0.37-0.56 s, short text answer <1 s; budget: Gemma Q4 2.97 GiB + projector 0.92 + KV/compute ~0.25 (GPU), Pocket TTS ~0.21 and web UI ~0.10 (CPU), Ubuntu ~1.20 = ~5.65 GiB. Audio goes natively into Gemma (no separate STT); TTS is Kyutai Pocket TTS GGUF, not Kokoro; the shipped default quant is UD-Q2_K_XL with Q4 optional. Its llama.cpp patch (llama-tts-server.patch) only adds a persistent /v1/audio/speech TTS server; it is not an audio-input fix. Pitfalls: NvMap 'error 12' unless page cache is dropped before load, mtmd allocates CUDA buffers even with -ngl 0. The NVIDIA HF blog (Apr 22, 2026) is a different pipeline: Orin Nano Super, native CUDA llama.cpp build, Parakeet STT + Kokoro TTS, Gemma text+vision only, and it says the prebuilt Jetson AI Lab Docker llama.cpp image 'is text-only. It doesn't load the vision projector' (a plausible, unconfirmed origin of NVIDIA's 'audio issue'). GitHub issue-search API found no llama.cpp issue about Gemma 4 audio on Jetson/Orin (39 hits for gemma4+audio+cuda, none of the visible ones Jetson-related). Net: the community result post-dates the NVIDIA note and uses a newer llama.cpp; still unmeasured on PC2 (JetPack 6.2 / L4T 36.4.3) and must be tested there.

verify.corrections: Five of six claims hold; change these assumptions. (1) Audio scope is wider than "ASR/AST only": E2B answers spoken questions and extracts JSON from spoken commands directly (verified live on this Mac: "What is the capital of France?" -> "Paris" with no text prompt; soda request -> {"object":"cold can of soda","location":"fridge"}, 232-511 ms wall). Design the voice loop as speech -> E2B -> action, not speech -> ASR -> text -> E2B. But multilingual S2TT on E2B was poor in a one-shot Spanish trial, so evaluate each demo language before promising translation on stage. (2) CoVoST: the model card (33.47/35.54/38.5) and tech report (35.4/38.2) disagree; cite one source. (3) llama.cpp: the BF16-mmproj rule is obsolete (root cause fixed Apr 13 by #21824; Q8_0 mmproj works and is 557 MB), #21625 was a prerequisite not a follow-up, Metal now has a ROLL kernel, and the current harness server already accepts audio (same model, no downloads), logging "audio input is in experimental stage". Audio is 25 tokens/s (official), must be mono 16 kHz, >30 s is chunked by llama.cpp but truncated by Transformers; identical clips are KV-cached, so rotate clips when timing. (4) NVIDIA's Orin note is undated, unlinked and E2B-only; the Aug 31 community repo runs native E2B audio on llama.cpp 9f0d017 (Aug 17, after all fixes) on an Orin Nano Super with 0.37-0.56 s TTFT, and its only llama.cpp patch is a TTS server. NVIDIA's own Docker llama.cpp image is text-only (no mmproj), a plausible but unconfirmed origin of the "issue". Plan a native CUDA (arch 87) build from a recent commit on PC2 first; vLLM gemma4-jetson-orin container is the fallback, and Ollama is reported not to work with Gemma 4 on Orin Nano. (5) Docs moved to gemma.ai; license is plain Apache 2.0 (GGUF metadata agrees). Note: the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so verification used direct fetches of official docs, GitHub/HF APIs, GGUF header parsing and a live server test.

research.area: LiteRT and LiteRT-LM platform support (as of 2026-10-18)

findings.claim: LiteRT-LM's current release is v0.18.0 (Oct 6, 2026); it installs on Jetson Orin NX without building because the `litert-lm-api` 0.18.0 bindings ship a `manylinux_2_27_aarch64` wheel (Python >=3.10) and the `litert-lm` CLI is a pure-Python `py3-none-any` wheel.
findings.evidence: PyPI lists litert_lm_api-0.18.0 wheels for win_amd64, manylinux_2_27_x86_64, manylinux_2_27_aarch64, macosx_12_0_arm64, android_23_arm64_v8a and android_23_x86_64, released Oct 6, 2026; the GitHub releases page marks v0.18.0 as latest (06 Oct). JetPack 6 is Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35, which satisfies manylinux_2_27.

findings.claim: LiteRT/LiteRT-LM have no CUDA or TensorRT path: GPU on Linux (x86_64 and arm64) is WebGPU via Dawn on Vulkan (`libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so`), Android is OpenCL/OpenGL, Apple is Metal, Windows is WebGPU on Direct3D; the official LiteRT-LM matrix lists GPU for Android/iOS/macOS/Windows/Linux and CPU-only for 'IoT'.
findings.evidence: The LiteRT 2.3.0 C++ SDK page (updated 2026-10-08) lists linux_arm64 (aarch64) prebuilts libLiteRt.so and libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so 'WebGPU (Vulkan)'; the LiteRT GPU page gives the same per-platform API table; LiteRT 2.1.0-2.3.0 release notes never mention CUDA or TensorRT. Issue #2570 confirms `prebuilt/linux_arm64` contains only the WebGPU accelerator.

findings.claim: Google's own Gemma 4 E2B model card benchmarks a Jetson Orin Nano with LiteRT-LM: CPU 109 prefill / 12.2 decode tok/s (TTFT 9.4 s for 1024 prompt tokens, 3681 MB) and GPU 1,142 prefill / 24.2 decode tok/s (TTFT 0.9 s, 2739 MB); Raspberry Pi 5 16GB CPU is 133 / 7.6 tok/s (TTFT 7.8 s, 1546 MB).
findings.evidence: The IoT table on litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm (1024 prefill / 256 decode tokens, 4 CPU threads, 2048 context) lists those rows; the Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ8 NPU row is 3,747 / 31.7 tok/s. Orin NX (8 cores at up to 2.0 GHz) should land somewhat above Orin Nano on CPU, but no Orin NX row is published.

findings.claim: The Jetson GPU path (WebGPU/Vulkan) is real but unreliable across versions: it worked from the pip wheel on an Orin NX 16 GB in April 2026 (`backend=litert_lm.Backend.GPU()`, ~1.9 s median for a short text command, ~3.0 GB RSS, ~5 s shader init per process), failed in GPU graph compilation for the official E2B bundle on Orin (JetPack 6, Vulkan 1.3.251) and Thor at v0.13.1/0.14.0 (issue closed without reproduction), and a Sep 14, 2026 report has E4B on GPU working on an Orin NX 16 GB only after downloading `prebuilt/linux_arm64` and setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
findings.evidence: Issue #2001 (Apr 20-21, 2026, Orin NX 16 GB, JetPack 36.x, litert-lm-api 0.10.1): maintainer whhone said 'The linux_aarch64 package should include the GPU .so' and the reporter confirmed Backend.GPU worked (text 1917 ms median, audio-to-JSON 2859 ms). Issue #2570 (Jun 15-Sep 14, 2026): SIGSEGV / silent exit on `--backend=gpu`, 'NVVM compilation failed: 3' on Orin Nano L4T R39.2, closed Jul 1 with 'build with Clang'; CPU worked in every report (Thor CPU 14-20 tok/s decode).

findings.claim: Gemma 4 LiteRT-LM bundles: `gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm` 2.58 GB and `gemma-4-E4B-it.litertlm` 3.65 GB (mixed 2/4/8-bit 'mobile quantization', text weights as low as 0.8 GB with 1.12 GB memory-mapped embeddings), vision and audio encoders inside the file and loaded on demand, 32k context supported, MTP drafter included (files downloaded before May 5, 2026 must be re-downloaded); 12B is supported since v0.17.0 (laptops), 26B/31B are not.
findings.evidence: HF model cards and the Gemma 4 page on developers.google.com state these sizes and 'LiteRT-LM supports E2B and E4B models today, with support for larger models coming soon'; v0.17.0 release notes (Sep 9) add Gemma 4 12B multimodal + MTP. The RTX 4090 row shows E2B at 11,234 / 143.4 tok/s on the Linux WebGPU path.

findings.claim: Gemma 4 E2B/E4B accept audio input (16 kHz mono float, max 30 s, 25 tokens per second of audio, multilingual ASR and speech translation) but produce no speech output; in LiteRT-LM Python you must pass `audio_backend=` and `vision_backend=` to `Engine(...)` or the process segfaults, and audio input has been reported working on Jetson Orin Nano CPU with litert-lm 0.14.0.
findings.evidence: Google's Gemma audio guide (updated 2026-10-10): 'Each second of audio is 25 tokens for Gemma 4', 'Audio supports a maximum length of 30 seconds', 'Sample Rate: 16kHz'. Issue #1848 was resolved by adding `litert_lm.Backend.CPU` for both modality backends (text ~1.75 s, audio ~5.4 s, vision ~22 s on a 4 GB x86 container). In #2570 the Orin Nano reporter wrote that text and audio input worked on a six-thread CPU server.

findings.claim: LiteRT-LM's Gemma 4 vision encoder costs several seconds per image on ARM CPUs at the default ~280-token budget (RK3588 8 threads: ~8.1 s CPU vs ~5.4 s Mali GPU for E2B; Qualcomm QCS8275: ~8 s CPU, ~20 s NPU), and the Python API exposes the fix: `Engine(max_vision_tokens_per_image=...)` plus `create_conversation(visual_token_budget=...)` with Gemma 4 options 70, 140, 280, 560 or 1120 tokens.
findings.evidence: Armbian blog (Sep 30, 2026, LiteRT-LM v0.17.1) reports E2B VL TTFT 8.9-9.4 s CPU/CPU vs 5.6-6.2 s GPU/GPU with ~280 vision tokens; issue #2187 (May 2026, open) reports 8 s CPU / 20 s NPU vision embedding. interfaces.py docstring: 'Image downscaling is currently only supported by Gemma4 models, whose budget options are 70, 140, 280, 560, or 1120.' No Jetson vision timing is published.

findings.claim: LiteRT-LM has first-class function calling and constrained decoding: Python `engine.create_conversation(tools=[python_fn])` derives the schema from docstrings/type hints and auto-executes tools (`automatic_tool_calling=True`, `approve_tool_call` hook); C++ `SetEnableConstrainedDecoding(true)` constrains tool-call syntax; LLGuidance supplies Regex / JSON Schema / Lark constraints, exposed in Python as `ResponseFormat.json(schema)` / `ResponseFormat.regex(pattern)` when `ConstrainedDecodingConfig(enable=True, provider=LL_GUIDANCE)` is set (ignored on turns that may call tools).
findings.evidence: Python API doc and conversation.py source (send_message(..., response_format=...), ValueError 'response_format cannot be used unless constrained_decoding_config with LL_GUIDANCE provider is set'); docs/api/cpp/constrained-decoding.md ('Supports Regex, JSON Schema, and Lark grammars', kRegex/kJsonSchema/kLark); tool-use.md (tools as JSON schema, parsed `tool_calls`). The overview says 'constrained decoding for improved accuracy' for tool use.

findings.claim: Do not build LiteRT-LM from source on the Jetson for tool calling: the prebuilt Linux `libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so` (x86_64 and arm64) uses a different libc++ ABI than a source-built runtime, so tool calls abort on the first constrained token (issue #3821, opened Oct 1, 2026, still open), while the PyPI `litert-lm-api` 0.17.1 wheels work on both architectures; the arm64 provider cannot be rebuilt from source (#2657).
findings.evidence: #3821: 'tool calls abort on the first constrained token'; reporter's disassembly shows unique_ptr trivial_abi and vector layout mismatches; maintainers labeled it a bug on Oct 5 and are investigating. #2657 (Jun 25, open) asks whether the arm64 provider can be rebuilt (it also uses 'ldaprb' instructions that fault on Cortex-A73).

findings.claim: Session/KV handling: a `Conversation` wraps a stateful `Session`, re-renders the Jinja chat template and sends only the new diff to the session (incremental prefill of history), `cache` = disk/memory/no controls KV and compilation caching, `cache_dir` stores compiled GPU artifacts; there is no public session-clone API in Python, and GPU engine creation costs ~5 s, so a demo must keep one persistent engine process.
findings.evidence: docs/api/cpp/conversation.md: Session 'is stateful, meaning it processes inputs incrementally'; the CLI configuration page documents `cache`, `max_num_tokens`, `cpu_thread_count`, `gpu_decode_steps_per_sync`; conversation.py has `cancel_process()` but no clone; issue #2001 measured ~5 s shader/engine init per `litert_lm_main` invocation on Orin NX.

findings.claim: Multi-token prediction (speculative decoding) is a one-flag speedup: `enable_speculative_decoding=True` in Python, `--enable-speculative-decoding=true` in the CLI, `speculative_decoding` in config.json; Google claims up to 2.2x decode on mobile GPUs and 1.5x on mobile CPUs (S26 Ultra E2B GPU 51.5 -> 66-92 tok/s by task), and the drafter is already inside the current E2B/E4B files.
findings.evidence: Gemma 4 LiteRT-LM page: 'up to 2.2x decode speedup on mobile GPUs' and 'up to 1.5x speedup on mobile CPUs', MTP 'universally recommended for all tasks on GPU backends'; the HF E2B card's speculative-decoding table and the May 5, 2026 re-download note.

findings.claim: Official Gemma 4 E2B LiteRT-LM numbers on consumer devices: Samsung S26 Ultra CPU 557/47 tok/s, GPU 3,808/52; iPhone 17 Pro GPU 2,878/56; MacBook Pro M4 Max GPU 7,835/160; Intel LunarLake GPU 3,751/48; E4B is roughly 2-3x slower everywhere (Pi 5 CPU 51/3.2 tok/s). No Gemma 4 benchmark row exists for any Pixel; the only Pixel row is EmbeddingGemma 2 on 'Pixel 11 Pro TPU' at 8.3 ms per text embedding.
findings.evidence: LiteRT-LM overview and models/gemma-4 pages (prefill/decode tables for E2B and E4B); the EmbeddingGemma 2 latency table lists 'Android (Pixel 11 Pro) TPU 8.3 ms text / 49 ms text+vision / 193.5 ms text+audio'.

findings.claim: Google's own 'LiteRT + Gemma on a robot' showcase (Aug 11, 2026) is a Reachy Mini driven by a Raspberry Pi 5 running YOLO on the VideoCore GPU, Moonshine speech recognition on CPU and Gemma 4 E2B via LiteRT-LM at 99 prefill / 9 decode tok/s and 1432 MB peak memory; Pi 5 GPU is supported in LiteRT (2.1.5) but a LiteRT-LM maintainer says the LLM GPU path on Pi 5 'works, although slower than its CPU'; Hailo AI HAT support is 'coming soon'.
findings.evidence: Google Developers Blog 'Mastering Edge AI on Raspberry Pi with LiteRT and Gemma' (install `pip install litert-cli`, run `litert lm run --from-huggingface-repo=litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm ... --attachment=image.jpg`); maintainer whhone's comment in issue #2001; LiteRT 2.1.5 notes 'Raspberry Pi 5 GPU acceleration'.

findings.claim: Pixel 11 / Tensor G6 is a supported LiteRT-LM NPU target on paper: the NPU page (updated 2026-09-02) lists a Gemma4-E2B build for Tensor_G6 (4-bit per-channel, 8192 context, 2642 MB) and Gemma3-1B for G5/G6, the Google Tensor SDK Beta (v2.1 released Oct 14, 2026; sign-up required) covers Tensor G5/G6, and its v1.02 sample app 'demonstrates running multimodal LLMs (for example, Gemma 4) on Google Pixel TPUs' with text, image and audio; no tokens/s for Gemma 4 on any Pixel is published.
findings.evidence: developers.google.com/edge/litert/next/litert_lm_npu model table; Tensor SDK release notes (v2.1 Oct 14, 2026; v2.0 Sep 2, 2026 'Tensor G6 ... available on Pixel 11 series'); Tensor SDK page says 'Sign up for access to Google Tensor SDK Beta' and host requirements are Linux x86_64 with Bazel 7.4.1. Pixel 11 launch (Aug 2026) is only confirmed by secondary news sites.

research.digest:
What exists. LiteRT is the renamed TensorFlow Lite runtime (2.3.0, Oct 7 2026; Python package ai-edge-litert) and LiteRT-LM (0.18.0, Oct 6 2026) is the LLM layer on top of it. It is now Google's only recommended on-device LLM path: the MediaPipe LLM Inference API is "maintenance-only" and the AI Edge Function Calling SDK is "Deprecated... migrate to LiteRT-LM". Install is `pip install litert-lm litert-lm-api` (Python >=3.10). The bindings ship manylinux_2_27 aarch64 wheels, so they install on the G1's Orin NX (JetPack 6, Ubuntu 22.04) with no build; do not build from source, the prebuilt constraint-provider library has an ABI mismatch that aborts tool calls (#3821). No jetson-containers package exists; pip is the route. APIs: Python, Kotlin and C++ stable; Swift and JS early preview. Models: litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm (2.58 GB) and E4B (3.65 GB), mixed 2/4/8-bit, vision and audio encoders inside the file and loaded on demand, 32k context, MTP drafter included; 12B is laptop-only; 26B/31B unsupported. Audio input is 16 kHz mono, 30 s max, 25 tokens/s, multilingual ASR and translation. It is input only: Gemma has no speech output, so a talking robot needs a separate on-device TTS.

Where it runs. CPU (XNNPACK) everywhere. GPU: OpenCL on Android, Metal on Apple, WebGPU (Dawn) over Vulkan on Linux x86_64/arm64 and Windows. NPU: Qualcomm, MediaTek, Google Tensor G5/G6, Intel, Samsung. There is no CUDA or TensorRT path in LiteRT or LiteRT-LM, so on Jetson the GPU is reachable only through Vulkan/WebGPU.

Jetson numbers. Google's E2B model card lists Jetson Orin Nano: CPU 109 prefill / 12.2 decode tok/s (TTFT 9.4 s on a 1024-token prompt), GPU 1,142 / 24.2 tok/s (TTFT 0.9 s, 2.7 GB). Community reality on Orin NX 16 GB: the pip wheel's GPU backend worked in April (about 1.9 s per short text command, 3 GB RSS, 5 s engine init), failed in WebGPU graph compilation for the official E2B bundle in June through August (issue closed without a fix), and in September E4B on GPU worked again only after downloading prebuilt/linux_arm64 and setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Treat Jetson CPU as reliable (expect roughly 12-18 tok/s with 8 threads) and Jetson GPU as "probably, after a day of testing". The one Jetson head-to-head (Thor) had llama.cpp CUDA at about 80 tok/s versus LiteRT-LM about 21 tok/s on CPU. Vision is the bigger problem for our loop: LiteRT-LM's Gemma 4 vision encoder costs about 8 s per image on ARM CPUs at the default ~280-token budget (RK3588, QCS8275), 5.4 s on a Mali GPU, and nobody has published Jetson vision timings. The Python API does expose our 70-token trick: Engine(max_vision_tokens_per_image=70) plus create_conversation(visual_token_budget=70), options 70/140/280/560/1120.

Features that matter. Tool use: pass plain Python functions as tools=[fn]; the runtime builds the schema from the docstring and auto-executes calls, with an approve_tool_call hook. Tool-call syntax is constrained natively, and LLGuidance adds Regex/JSON-schema/Lark constraints: ResponseFormat.json(schema) with ConstrainedDecodingConfig(provider=LL_GUIDANCE). Thinking is a per-message toggle with a token budget (0 = off). MTP (enable_speculative_decoding) is claimed at up to 2.2x on GPU, 1.5x on CPU. `litert-lm serve` is an OpenAI-compatible server (port 9379; streaming chat completions and, since 0.18.0, /v1/embeddings). Gotchas: always pass audio_backend and vision_backend or Python segfaults; keep one persistent engine (5 s init); config lives in ~/.litert-lm/config.json (backend, cpu_thread_count, cache, max_num_tokens, thinking...).

Other hardware. Raspberry Pi 5: E2B at 133/7.6 tok/s CPU (Google's Aug 2026 blog: 99/9 tok/s, 1.4 GB), and Google's own showcase is a Reachy Mini robot on a Pi 5 running YOLO (GPU) + Moonshine ASR + Gemma 4 E2B through LiteRT-LM, the closest public precedent to our demo. Pixel 11 (Tensor G6): a Gemma 4 E2B NPU build exists (4-bit, 8192 ctx, 2.6 GB), the Tensor SDK Beta v2.1 (Oct 14 2026, sign-up required) includes a sample app running multimodal Gemma 4 on the Pixel TPU, but no Gemma 4 tok/s is published for any Pixel; EmbeddingGemma 2 on Pixel 11 Pro TPU embeds text in 8.3 ms.

Recommendation. Keep llama.cpp+CUDA as the sub-second perception loop on the Orin (our measured path; LiteRT-LM cannot match it) and give LiteRT-LM a separate, visible job judges can point at: (1) the speech and planning brain on the Orin, Gemma 4 E2B via litert-lm-api with 30-s audio clips (multilingual commands) emitting tool calls under constrained decoding, running on CPU with GPU as a bonus; (2) EmbeddingGemma 2 (485 MB, text+image+audio) via LiteRT-LM as the robot's on-device memory/search of what it has seen and heard; (3) optionally a Pi 5 or Pixel 11 companion running Gallery/LiteRT-LM as the user-facing concierge terminal (Pi 5 for the Raspberry Pi prize at ~8 tok/s; Pixel for Best in Show/TPU, unverified). Day-1 test on the Orin: pip install, run E2B on CPU with --cpu-thread-count=8 under MAXN, then --backend=gpu (fallback: prebuilt/linux_arm64 + LD_LIBRARY_PATH), measure text, a 3-s wav and an image at visual_token_budget 70 vs 280. GPU working means ~24 tok/s and sub-second TTFT for short prompts; CPU only means ~12-15 tok/s and multi-second vision, fine for speech and planning, not for the fast loop.

checks.claim: LiteRT/LiteRT-LM have no CUDA or TensorRT path: Linux GPU (x86_64 and arm64) is WebGPU via Dawn on Vulkan (libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so), Android is OpenCL/OpenGL, Apple is Metal, Windows is WebGPU on Direct3D; the official LiteRT-LM matrix lists GPU for Android/iOS/macOS/Windows/Linux and CPU-only for IoT.
checks.note: LiteRT C++ SDK page (updated 2026-10-08, LiteRT 2.3.0) lists linux_arm64 prebuilts libLiteRt.so and libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so 'WebGPU (Vulkan)', Android libLiteRtClGlAccelerator.so 'OpenCL + OpenGL', macOS/iOS Metal, Windows 'WebGPU (Direct3D)'; the GPU page (2026-10-08) gives the same table; neither mentions CUDA or TensorRT. LiteRT release notes v2.1.0rc1 through v2.3.0 (07 Oct) never mention CUDA, TensorRT, NVIDIA or Jetson; v2.1.0 says 'Provided Desktop GPU backends prebuilt for Linux (x64, arm64)' with 'WebGPU/Dawn and OpenCL', v2.1.2 added Linux Python GPU 'through WebGPU'. The LiteRT-LM overview (2026-10-06) matrix: Android/iOS/macOS/Windows/Linux GPU yes, IoT GPU no. prebuilt/linux_arm64 holds libLiteRt.so, libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so, libwebgpu_dawn.so, libLiteRtTopKWebGpuSampler.so, libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so and nothing CUDA/OpenCL. Issue #2338 (DGX Spark/Thor/Orin support) was closed Jul 1, 2026 as a duplicate of #2570 with no NVIDIA-backend roadmap. Note the contradiction: the official matrix says IoT has no GPU while the E2B model card publishes a Jetson Orin Nano GPU row; treat Jetson GPU as unsupported-but-possible.

checks.claim: Google's Gemma 4 E2B model card benchmarks a Jetson Orin Nano with LiteRT-LM: CPU 109 prefill / 12.2 decode tok/s (TTFT 9.4 s, 3681 MB) and GPU 1,142 / 24.2 tok/s (TTFT 0.9 s, 2739 MB); Raspberry Pi 5 16GB CPU is 133 / 7.6 tok/s (TTFT 7.8 s, 1546 MB).

Caveats: the developers.google.com Gemma 4 page (updated 2026-09-04) reproduces the other rows but omits the Jetson rows; the card does not state the JetPack/L4T, power mode or LiteRT-LM version behind the Orin Nano numbers, and the E4B card has no Jetson row at all (RPi 5: 51 / 3.2 tok/s, TTFT 20.5 s). The 'Orin NX lands above Orin Nano' extrapolation is the researcher's, not published; NVIDIA's spec table did not parse cleanly on this pass, so the 8-core/2.0 GHz figure is unverified here.

checks.claim: The Jetson GPU path (WebGPU/Vulkan) is real but unreliable across versions: it worked from the pip wheel on an Orin NX 16 GB in April 2026 (~1.9 s median text command, ~3.0 GB RSS, ~5 s shader init), failed in GPU graph compilation for the official E2B bundle on Orin (JetPack 6, Vulkan 1.3.251) and Thor at v0.13.1/0.14.0 (closed without reproduction), and a Sep 14, 2026 report has E4B on GPU working on an Orin NX 16 GB only after downloading prebuilt/linux_arm64 and setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
checks.note: Confirmed by versioned community reports, with corrections. #2001 (Apr 20-21, 2026; Orin NX 16 GB, Ubuntu 22.04, JetPack 36.x, Python 3.10, litert-lm-api 0.10.1): whhone wrote 'The linux_aarch64 package should include the GPU .so'; reporter confirmed Backend.GPU with median 1917 ms text and 2859 ms audio-to-JSON (audio_backend=CPU). The '3.0 GB RSS' is actually 'system memory drop on engine load 3052 MB' (vs 1885 MB for a C++ wrapper, blamed on the wheel registering both libLiteRtGpuAccelerator.so and libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.so); the ~5 s init figure was for one-shot litert_lm_main, not the wheel. #2570 (Jun 15, 2026): official E2B bundle on Orin (L4T R36 rev 5.0/JetPack 6, Vulkan 1.3.251) and Thor (JetPack 7, Vulkan 1.4.315) at v0.13.1 and main exits 0 with no generation during GPU delegate graph compilation; multimodal fine-tune SIGSEGVs; Jul 13 Orin Nano 8 GB on L4T R39.2.0/Ubuntu 24.04 with the 0.14.0 wheel: 'NVVM compilation failed: 3', Dawn pipeline errors, exit 139; maintainer ztenghui only asked 'Could you try to use Clang to build' and closed Jul 1; reporter answered they already used Clang-18 and the crash is in the prebuilt stripped .so, with no further maintainer reply; Thor via Python still failed Aug 16. Sep 14 (yegorius): 'PyPi package doesn't ship prebuilt binaries from prebuilt/linux_arm64', workaround LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./linux_arm64 litert-lm run --backend=gpu gemma4-e4b, E4B GPU works on Orin NX 16 GB; no version or JetPack stated. Likely mechanism the researcher missed: python/litert_lm/BUILD bundles only libLiteRt, libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator, libLiteRtTopKWebGpuSampler, libGemmaModelConstraintProvider + liblitert-lm into Linux wheels, not libwebgpu_dawn.so, whose history in prebuilt/linux_arm64 starts Jun 8, 2026 (after the April success). Unverified: whether the accelerator dynamically needs Dawn; check with ldd on the robot.

checks.claim: Gemma 4 E2B/E4B accept audio input (16 kHz mono float, max 30 s, 25 tokens per second, multilingual ASR and speech translation) but produce no speech output; in LiteRT-LM Python you must pass audio_backend= and vision_backend= to Engine(...) or the process segfaults, and audio input has been reported working on Jetson Orin Nano CPU with litert-lm 0.14.0.
checks.note: Audio spec is official: ai.google.dev audio page (updated 2026-10-10, now marked deprecated in favor of gemma.ai) says 'Sample Rate: 16kHz', mono, float32 in [-1, 1], 'Audio supports a maximum length of 30 seconds', 'Each second of audio is 25 tokens for Gemma 4', ASR and speech translation, with 'Gemma 4 E2B, E4B, and 12B Unified' trained for speech; the Gemma 4 model card (2026-07-30) gives audio input only for E2B/E4B/12B Unified (26B A4B and 31B are text+image) and describes output as 'generating text output' with no speech output. LiteRT-LM Python docs (2026-09-04) document backend=, vision_backend=, audio_backend= (e.g. audio_backend=litert_lm.Backend.CPU()); engine.py defaults both to None and passes None to the C API with no validation. The segfault itself comes from issue #1848 (Apr 3, 2026, Linux x86_64 Docker, 'latest' PyPI wheel with no version number, closed as user error: text ~1.75 s, audio ~5.4 s for 3 s WAV, vision ~22 s on a 4 GB CPU instance); whether 0.18.0 still crashes rather than raising is unverified. Orin Nano audio on CPU is confirmed by #2570 (Jul 13, 2026: 0.14.0 aarch64 wheel, L4T R39.2.0, 'text and audio input' worked on a six-thread CPU server). Extra facts: v0.14.0 added 'NPU and GPU audio acceleration' and CLI auto backend selection; #2001 ran audio_backend=CPU alongside Backend.GPU for text on the Orin NX.

verify.corrections: Change these assumptions. (1) LiteRT-LM GPU on the Orin NX is officially unsupported, not merely flaky: the LiteRT-LM matrix (updated 2026-10-06) lists IoT as CPU-only, the only Linux arm64 accelerator is WebGPU via Dawn on Vulkan, and both Jetson issues (#2570, #2338) were closed in July 2026 without a fix. The one positive report (Sep 14, E4B, LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at a downloaded prebuilt/linux_arm64) names no version. A plausible cause the researcher missed: python/litert_lm/BUILD bundles only libLiteRt, libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator, libLiteRtTopKWebGpuSampler, libGemmaModelConstraintProvider and liblitert-lm into the Linux wheels, not libwebgpu_dawn.so, which appeared in prebuilt/linux_arm64 around Jun 8, 2026, after the April success on 0.10.1. Day-one test on the robot: pip install litert-lm, ldd the accelerator, retry GPU with LD_LIBRARY_PATH at the prebuilt directory. Keep llama.cpp/CUDA as the sub-second perception engine; budget LiteRT-LM CPU near the Orin Nano figures (E2B 109/12.2 tok/s, 9.4 s TTFT at 1024 tokens) unless GPU works, and try enable_ynnpack (arm64 wheels build with YNNPACK since v0.16.0). (2) Larger Gemma 4 bundles exist: 12B (6.9 GB, text+vision+audio, v0.17+, ~7.5 GB GPU memory) and text-only 26B A4B/31B (15.8/19.2 GB, desktop v0.17.1+ and web, GPU only); none fits the Orin plan. (3) Audio is input-only on E2B/E4B/12B (16 kHz, 30 s, 25 tok/s); speech output needs separate TTS. (4) JetPack 7.2/7.2.1 (L4T 39.2, Ubuntu 24.04) now covers the Orin family, but an Orin Nano on R39.2 also failed on GPU in July, so do not upgrade six days out expecting a fix. (5) Pre-download every bundle and wheel; the event forbids cloud. ai.google.dev Gemma docs are marked deprecated in favor of gemma.ai. research.digest:
What we actually own. The robot is a G1 EDU with the 23-DoF body (waist yaw only, wrist roll only, no head joints), two BrainCo Revo 2 five-finger hands on USB-serial, a Livox Mid-360 and RealSense D435i in the head, and PC2 = Jetson Orin NX 16 GB on JetPack 6.2 (Ubuntu 22.04). Everything we need for a voice + vision + gesture + grasp demo is reachable from Python on PC2 through unitree_sdk2py over DDS on eth0 (192.168.123.164, unitree/123). The hackathon rule "no cloud" is satisfiable: the factory GPT voice assistant must be turned off, but ASR, TTS, LEDs, locomotion, gestures and hands are all local.

Audio. The head has a 4-mic array, a 3 W (5 W peak) speaker and an RGB LED bar. From PC2, AudioClient (service "voice") gives offline TTS (TtsMaker, speaker_id 1 = English, 0 = Chinese), raw PCM playback (PlayStream, 16 kHz mono 16-bit, 50 ms chunks work), volume and LedControl(R,G,B) (>= 200 ms apart). Raw mic audio arrives as 16 kHz mono PCM on multicast 239.168.123.161:5555 in 160 ms packets once the mic is enabled (community drivers call voice API 1008 {"mode":1}); the built-in offline ASR also publishes JSON on rt/audio_msg with a 0-180 deg direction-of-arrival angle, which is a cheap "turn toward the speaker" cue. Community round trip mic-to-speaker is 200-250 ms. The onboard speaker is small; for a loud hall a USB speaker on one of PC2's three USB-C 3.0 host ports is a sensible add, as is a USB webcam if we want a second viewpoint (the D435i is held by Unitree's video_hub_pc4 service, which we already know how to stop via mscli).

Motion. LocoClient (service "sport") does Damp, Start (FSM 500), Move(vx,vy,vyaw) with a 1 s auto-stop unless continuous, SetVelocity with duration, HighStand/LowStand, Squat2StandUp, and arm tasks WaveHand/ShakeHand. G1ArmActionClient (service "arm") plays 15 preset gestures by id (26 high wave, 27 shake hand, 19 hug, 17 clap, 18 high five, 20 heart, 11-13 kisses, 99 release). Custom arm motion is LowCmd on rt/arm_sdk at 50 Hz (weight at index 29, kp 60/kd 1.5 in the official example) while the built-in controller keeps balance; it only works in locked-stand or run-control FSM 500/501 and requires ServiceSwitch("g1_arm_example", 0) first. Hands: brainco_hand_service bridges each hand to rt/brainco/{left,right}/cmd as six 0..1 positions (0 open, 1 closed) at 100 Hz; grip >= 50 N and 100 mm opening comfortably hold a can; no tactile data over that bridge.

Numbers that shape the plan. 35 kg, folds to 690x450x300 mm, ships in a wheeled suitcase (two people to pack; rental firms move it in a ~50 kg case in an SUV). Battery 9000 mAh, about 2 h; with the GPU busy expect less, so plan charging between judge rounds. EDU arm load ~3 kg. Odometry on rt/odommodestate at 500 Hz, lidar cloud at 10 Hz. SLAM nav exists but needs a pre-built map, straight-line goals <= 10 m and obstacles >= 50 cm, so it is not a drop-in obstacle avoider.

Gotchas. (1) Firmware gating: on robot software 1.5.3 in walk-run mode (R2+A, FSM 802) SetFsmId/Move returned 0 and did nothing and the sport lease failed (code 3102); use regular mode R1+X (FSM 500) and verify on day one. (2) Debug mode (L2+R2) kills the ai_sport service until reboot; never enter it during the demo. (3) L2+B is the e-stop at any time, but the robot collapses; a fall with BrainCo hands probably breaks fingers (Unitree warns against lying/squat boot with hands fitted). Keep the R3 remote bound and in a human's hand; the robot even reports an error if the remote times out. (4) Wi-Fi: DDS must stay on eth0; PC2's onboard Wi-Fi is flaky, so use the owner's MT7612U USB AP (SSH at 10.42.0.1) or a travel router, never venue Wi-Fi. (5) Memory: 16 GB unified; a community voice stack on this exact board once OOM-killed its LLM, so budget VLM + STT + TTS together and run headless. (6) Reflashing to JetPack 7.2 or enabling MAXN_SUPER (157 TOPS/40 W) is possible with legion1581's tool but is a multi-hour, roll-back-needing risk six days out; only do it if the runtime team shows a decisive gain.

Recommendation for the G1 side. Script, do not train. A state machine on PC2 owns safety and sequencing; Gemma supplies perception answers and intent (one direct question per frame, as the harness already proves). Day 1: confirm firmware, FSM 500 locomotion via SDK, ASR/TTS/LED calls, hands open/close, camera access. Then build five skills: listen (multicast mic, LED blue), speak (TtsMaker or PlayStream, LED green), face/approach (DOA angle or VLM bearing -> Move with 1 s pulses, odometry for distance, lidar min-range guard), gesture (ExecuteAction ids), and grasp/handover (arm_sdk joint trajectory recorded from the real robot at the real table height, BrainCo close to ~0.7, lift, then ShakeHand-style extension and open). Rehearse with the robot on its stand first, then on a flat clear floor with a spotter on L2+B. Avoid walk-run mode, stairs, crowds within arm reach, and long arm extensions while stepping.
open_questions: Which robot software/firmware version is on our G1 and does LocoClient locomotion work on it? Test: boot to R1+X (FSM 500), run example/g1/high_level/g1_loco_client_example.py on PC2 (python3 g1_loco_client_example.py eth0), check GetFsmId() == 500 and that Move(0.3,0,0) actually moves; if it returns 0 without motion we are in the issue-#170 situation and need the 1->4->501 workaround or a different FSM.

Does the built-in offline ASR on rt/audio_msg recognize English, and what wake/mode setting enables the raw multicast mic stream on our firmware? Test: enable wake mode (L2+Select or the app), subscribe to rt/audio_msg and listen on 239.168.123.161:5555 from PC2; if English ASR is poor, run our own STT on the multicast PCM.

Does LedControl override the firmware's FSM status colors (blue/orange/yellow) while running, and does the voice service's own breathing-LED behavior interfere? Test: call LedControl(255,0,0) in FSM 500 and observe for 10 s.

Are our BrainCo hands the Basic or Touch (tactile) edition, and are both detected? Test: ls /dev/ttyUSB*, run brainco_hand_server then test_brainco_hand_server left/right; check stark-sdk device type in the service log.

What is the usable reach and the comfortable grasp height of the 23-DoF arm at a given table height, and does a right-arm extension plus 0.4 kg can perturb balance while standing (FSM 500)? Test: with the robot suspended, replay the arm7/arm5 arm_sdk example toward a mock table pose, then repeat on the floor with a spotter, logging rt/lowstate.

Can the head RealSense be used while Unitree's video_hub_pc4 is stopped without breaking the app, and does the DDS topic rt/frontvideostream offer frames without stopping it? Test: mscli stopservice video_hub_pc4, open the camera with pyrealsense2 at 640x480; separately subscribe to rt/frontvideostream and inspect the payload.

Real battery runtime with the GPU loaded: measure batteryPower from rt/slam_info (or the app) over a 30 min rehearsal with llama-server, STT and TTS running; decide whether a spare battery is needed for the judging window.

Is MAXN_SUPER (40 W) already available on our JetPack 6.2 install (sudo nvpmodel -q; nvpmodel -p --verbose) or only after a --super reflash, and does the carrier stay cool under it? Test: tegrastats for 20 min at MAXN with the model loaded.

Does the arm action service's shake-hand pose (id 27) or LocoClient.ShakeHand() work as a handover posture together with an independent BrainCo open command, and what is the 7404 restriction set in FSM 500 on our firmware? Test: GetActionList() and try ids 27, 26, 19 in FSM 500.

Transport logistics: does our suitcase plus the hands fit in the owner's vehicle and who are the two people lifting on 10/24? Measure the case; also confirm the venue has a flat hard floor area roughly 3x3 m for walking demos.

checks.claim: Raw microphone audio reaches PC2 as denoised 16 kHz mono s16le PCM over UDP multicast 239.168.123.161:5555 (5120-byte packets = 160 ms) once the voice service is put in 'mic on' mode (app/remote wake mode, or RPC API 1008 {"mode":1} on service "voice" per community drivers); the built-in offline ASR publishes JSON on DDS topic rt/audio_msg with text, confidence, language and a 0-180 deg direction-of-arrival angle.
checks.note: Official (live VuiClient page): '在麦克风打开状态下(可使用APP或者遥控器切换到唤醒模式)，在组播地址239.168.123.161 端口5555会输出降噪后的音频数据。音频数据格式为单通道/16K采样率/16bit'; rt/audio_msg is a std_msgs::msg::dds_::String_ carrying JSON {index, timestamp, text, angle (方位角度 0-180), speaker_id, sense, confidence, language, is_final}, ASR '默认非流式模型，本地离线式', with the warning '部分字段在开发中'. The same topic also carries {"play_state":0|1} messages, so parsers must handle both shapes. Community-only parts: 5120-byte/160 ms packets, API 1007 get-mode / 1008 set-mode {"mode":1} (mode 2 = off, default) and the ~160 ms / 200-250 ms latencies come from experientialtech/g1-audio-driver (created 2026-02, 9 stars, names no firmware version); 1007/1008 do not exist in any official SDK header, and the official page says the mic is enabled only via APP or remote. PiotrG1996/unitree_converse (fork of SaxionMechatronics, pushed 2026-10-16) joins the same group on the Jetson at 192.168.123.164. Discrepancy to measure on PC2: Unitree's own example reads with a 2048-byte buffer, which would truncate 5120-byte datagrams; print recvfrom() lengths before trusting either number.

checks.claim: The factory voice assistant (wake word, chat, music) is GPT-based and needs internet, so it must be switched off for the 'no cloud anywhere in the loop' rule; the ASR and TTS engines themselves run offline on PC1 and are fine to use.
checks.note: Official voice-assistant page (live): 'G1设备已经接入GPT模型（固件版本≥1.3.0）。连接互联网后，开启语音助手对话模式，设备可支持基于GPT模型的语音对话（例如聊天、动作、音乐播放等）'; switch via remote 'L1+L2' or APP '【设备】-【数据】-【音频】-【语音助手】'; wake word 笨笨同学, L2+Select wakes, L1+Select interrupts; '关闭交互: 程序休眠，停止录音'. ASR/TTS are '本地离线' per the VuiClient page. 'On PC1' is inference, not official text: PC2's master_service snapshot has no vui_service, the architecture page says PC1 is Unitree's closed motion-control computer, and g1-audio-driver says the mic array/speaker hang off PC1. Two corrections: (1) 'switch it off' conflicts with claim 3: the multicast mic stream exists only in the assistant's mic-on/wake mode, and 关闭交互 stops recording; (2) without internet the assistant does not die, it falls back to an offline mode ('如果GPT未联网，会回复"你好，我在呢"，即进入离线语音交互模式'), so it will still wake on the wake word or L2+Select, talk, breathe the LEDs (blue on voice, green after wake) and may run built-in offline commands while your pipeline is also using TTS and LEDs. Also note some questions trigger web search when online, and the architecture page says cloud (MQTT/OTA/WebRTC TURN) is used once the user has authorised it.

verify.corrections: Change these assumptions. (1) Do not plan to "switch off" the factory voice assistant: Unitree's official page says the 239.168.123.161:5555 mic stream only flows while the mic is on, i.e. in the assistant's wake-conversation mode (APP or L1+L2), and 关闭交互 stops recording. Either way the offline assistant still wakes on 笨笨同学 / L2+Select, speaks, drives the LEDs and may run built-in commands, so test speaker/LED contention before demo day. (2) Measure the multicast datagram size on PC2: Unitree's own example reads 2048-byte buffers, the community driver assumes 5120. rt/audio_msg also carries {"play_state"} messages. (3) Confirm vui_service >= 2.0.3.8 and vui module >= 2.0.0.3 in the app service list; the voice service runs on PC1, not PC2. (4) Issue #170 is a 29-DoF, 3-DoF-waist unit on software 1.5.3 where the regular mode is 501 (R1+Y); on the 23-DoF unit it is 500 (R1+X). Record the robot's software version now, test SetVelocity in FSM 500 on day one, keep the 1->4->501 sequence (xr_teleoperate PR #312, unmerged) as fallback, and try the newly documented SwitchToUserCtrl/SwitchToInternalCtrl user mode. (6) Never press L2+R2 during the demo; it kills ai_sport until reboot. L2+B damp stays the e-stop.
